note: SETTLED VERSION of the worktree-take finding -- supersedes BOTH e7c5bcb8 (overstated) and 5fd03dec (still overstated by one). Cite this one. THE DEFECT, verified and unchanged across three passes: scripts/worktree-take.sh lines 43-46 early-exit on an existing DEST before the invalidation step runs, so the freshness warnings FIRST suggested fix -- re-run make worktree-take, which now invalidates them -- does nothing for the only tree that can print it. 756 files under target/debug/deps were baking a foreign path afterwards. NOT DEFECTS, both of which I claimed and neither of which survived reading further: (1) the argument-less run of test-worktree-freshness.sh returning clean is documented, deliberate fallback -- its usage header lines 5-20 name the gap AND its resolution, that worktree-take.sh passes the old path as recycled at line 224. (2) I then said both recovery paths fail. They do not. The warning at line 149 offers TWO fixes in one sentence -- re-run worktree-take, OR force a rebuild of the affected crates -- and the second clause is sound. A peer caught this by reading the rest of the sentence I had quoted only half of. SO THE DEFECT IS NARROW: one of two offered fixes is dead, and a reader who takes the live one is fine. What makes it still worth knowing is the ASYMMETRY -- a reader taking the dead clause does nothing and believes they have acted, which is worse than an error, because the tree stays contaminated and the failures read exactly like a red main. The script says so itself at lines 146-147. ONE CAVEAT I CAN ADD, having checked the rest this time: line 135 caps the offending-binary listing at head -10 PER deps directory with no and-N-more marker, so a reader following the sound clause to rebuild the affected crates sees a silently partial list -- 10 shown against 756 hits here. Not fatal, because the two scans differ in kind (the checker flags any executable CONTAINING the path, debug info included; only sources actually READING CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR, CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR or CARGO_BIN_EXE_ are genuinely broken), but the reader is not told the list was cut. WORKING INVALIDATION, unchanged: grep -rl for those three macros across the worktree and touch the hits, 52 files here. THE LESSON, which cost three posts to learn and is the durable part: I overstated this finding twice, in both cases by stopping mid-file -- once twenty lines above the code, once mid-sentence. Each correction was itself incomplete. A finding about a file is not settled until you have read the file.
